Saffron Rice Cake With Barberries And Chicken

Served at: Yalda Night

Serves 6Prep 30 minCook 1 hr 15 min

This traditional Persian dish, known as 'Tahchin,' is a festive saffron-infused rice cake layered with tender chicken and tangy barberries. It is often served during Yalda Night, the celebration of the longest night of the year, symbolizing warmth and togetherness with its vibrant colors and rich flavors.

Ingredients

  • 3 cups basmati rice (about 600 g)
  • 2 large chicken breasts
  • 1 large onion, thinly sliced
  • 1/2 cup plain yogurt (120 ml)
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground saffron threads, dissolved in 2 tablespoons hot water
  • 1/2 cup dried barberries (zereshk) (75 g)
  • 3 tablespoons unsalted butter
  • 1/4 cup vegetable oil
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper
  • 1/2 teaspoon turmeric
  • 2 tablespoons sugar
  • 1/4 cup slivered almonds or pistachios (optional, for garnish)

Method

  1. Rinse the basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear; soak in water for 30 minutes, then drain.
  2. In a pot, bring water to a boil with a pinch of salt; parboil the rice for 5-6 minutes until slightly tender but still firm; drain and set aside.
  3. In a skillet, heat 1 tablespoon oil and sauté the sliced onions until golden and soft; add turmeric and stir for 1 minute.
  4. Add chicken breasts, salt, and pepper to the skillet; cook until the chicken is fully cooked and lightly browned; remove and shred the chicken once cooled.
  5. In a small pan, melt 1 tablespoon butter; add barberries and sugar, sauté gently for 2-3 minutes until plump; remove from heat and set aside.
  6. In a large bowl, whisk together yogurt, eggs, dissolved saffron with its water, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil.
  7. Add half of the parboiled rice to the yogurt mixture and mix gently to coat the rice evenly.
  8. Grease a 9-inch (23 cm) round baking dish with butter and oil mixture.
  9. Spread half of the saffron-coated rice evenly in the bottom of the dish, pressing down gently to form a layer.
  10. Layer the shredded chicken evenly over the rice, then sprinkle half of the sautéed onions and half of the barberries over the chicken.
  11. Top with the remaining saffron rice, pressing down gently to compact the layers.
  12. Cover the dish tightly with aluminum foil and bake in a preheated 350°F (175°C) oven for 1 hour.
  13. Remove the foil and bake for an additional 10-15 minutes to crisp the top layer.
  14. Let the rice cake cool for 10 minutes, then invert onto a serving platter so the golden crust is on top.
  15. Garnish with remaining sautéed onions, barberries, and slivered almonds or pistachios if desired before serving.

Tips

  • Soaking the rice and parboiling helps achieve a fluffy texture and prevents overcooking during baking.
  • Handle barberries gently as they can be bitter; sautéing with sugar balances their tartness.
  • For a vegetarian version, substitute chicken with sautéed mushrooms or eggplant.
